verdict_reason: the EMA family cannot be frozen on a 1m base without overruling the charter's one_minute_role clause. Everything else is resolved and recorded.

parameter_provenance_registry.evidence: the dominant EMA family in this codebase by a wide margin — e9 164, e200 148, e20 137, e50 122 occurrences; the ribbon periods are vestigial beside them
parameter_provenance_registry.existing_coarse_parents: already defined at 15m / 1H / 4H by the MTF EMA stack work, so this family DOES have coarse-TF parents
parameter_provenance_registry.blocked_because: a 1m-native EMA of these periods would still have no coarse-TF parent; only the coarse-TF definitions are admissible
parameter_provenance_registry.admissible_form: EMA defined at 15m / 1H / 1D per the charter's aggregation_contract, with 1m used to time when the coarse condition first became true

parameter_provenance_registry.evidence: near-vestigial in code — EMA89 8, ewm(span=89) 3, ewm(span=34) 2, EMA21 2, ewm(span=8) 1
parameter_provenance_registry.not_carried_forward: not pre-registered for this programme; using it later requires a new hypothesis family with its own multiplicity treatment

parameter_provenance_registry.superseded_by: slot-RVOL and CUM-RVOL, which are charter-named families whose baseline membership is already frozen
parameter_provenance_registry.why: a flat 20-bar mean ignores minute-of-session shape entirely, and the charter's own rationale for slot baselines is exactly that

parameter_provenance_registry.frozen_rule: the per-slot baseline is computed over OBSERVED and STRUCTURAL_NO_TRADE minutes only; UNOBSERVED minutes are excluded from both numerator and denominator
parameter_provenance_registry.coarse_parent: session-level volume state; 1m measures WHEN within the session it is reached

parameter_provenance_registry.frozen_rule: a cumulative curve crossing an UNOBSERVED minute is flagged from that point forward for that session

registry_resolution.method: occurrence inventory across the codebase plus a read of the frozen charter; conflicting historical implementations were NOT merged
registry_resolution.charter_wins: the charter names slot-RVOL and CUM-RVOL as feature families and their baseline semantics are already frozen, so they take precedence over the legacy 20-bar volume ratio

blocking_conflict.severity: BLOCKING — this is why the verdict is HOLD
blocking_conflict.discovered: while checking whether the charter already fixed parameters, as the gate instructed
blocking_conflict.quoted_enforcement: the FEATURE / CLOCK DICTIONARY must name, for every 1m-derived quantity, the coarser-TF definition it measures. A 1m quantity with no coarse-TF parent is inadmissible by construction.
quoted_forbidden: searching for thresholds, patterns or rules AT 1m granularity
promoting any 1m-native construct to a signal
using 1m to redefine a coarse-TF state after seeing outcomes
blocking_conflict.quoted_rationale: 1m over a decade of S&P 500 names is on the order of 10^9 bars. An unrestricted search there would generate a multiplicity burden that no deflation procedure could honestly absorb. Restricting 1m to MEASUREMENT of already-fixed definitions keeps the number of inferential claims tied to the coarse-TF layer, where it is countable.
blocking_conflict.consequence: an EMA over 1-minute closes with an N-minute span has no coarse-TF parent. It is not a measurement of a 15m/1H/1D object; it is a new 1m-native object, and the charter calls that inadmissible by construction.
blocking_conflict.why_not_overruled_here: freezing 1m EMA periods would silently overrule a sealed charter, and the charter's stated reason for the clause is the multiplicity burden of searching ~10^9 bars — the exact failure this programme exists to prevent

also_relevant.feature_families_status: NAMED ONLY — the dictionary that defines them, with each one's coarse-TF parent and determinable-at rule, is a later step and is not frozen here
also_relevant.note: the FEATURE / CLOCK DICTIONARY is itself listed as not yet frozen, and this gate is a legitimate place to write it — but it must obey one_minute_role while doing so

prerequisite_missing.why: Builder Spec V2 deliberately set higher_timeframe_rule.aggregated_in_v2 = false, so no coarse bars exist yet for a coarse EMA to be defined on
prerequisite_missing.already_specified_by: the charter's aggregation_contract, which fixes the hierarchy, left-closed left-labelled boundaries, session-aligned 1H with a flagged 30-minute stub, and the UNOBSERVED_CONTAMINATED propagation rule
prerequisite_missing.so: the aggregation gate is specified but not built

options.name: build the coarse aggregation layer first, then define EMA there
options.effect: EMA is defined at 15m/1H/1D from the same 1m atoms; the 1m layer times when a coarse EMA condition first became true
options.cost: one additional build gate before features
options.why_recommended: it is what the charter already contemplates, the aggregation contract is already frozen in detail, and it keeps the countable inferential claims at the coarse layer where multiplicity can be deflated honestly

options.name: amend one_minute_role to admit a named 1m-native EMA family
options.effect: 1m EMA periods become admissible as an explicitly registered hypothesis family
options.cost: the new family carries its own multiplicity and provenance burden, and the ~10^9-bar search-space rationale must be answered rather than bypassed
options.why_not_recommended: it reopens the constraint that keeps this programme's claim count countable; it should be a deliberate decision, never a side effect of a feature spec

blocking_conflict.rvol_may_proceed: both RVOL families have session-level coarse parents and already have their missing-data semantics frozen; nothing in this conflict prevents them

causal_timestamp_contract.rule: a feature value at regular minute t may use only information available through the close of minute t
causal_timestamp_contract.observability: a state using feature[t] is known only AFTER bar t completes
causal_timestamp_contract.forbidden_shortcut: treating a close-derived feature as executable at the same bar's open, or at a price already used to construct it
causal_timestamp_contract.charter_alignment: NO D+1 INFORMATION MAY ENTER FORMATION X. Persistence is an OUTCOME, never a feature.

forbidden: skip the minute and pretend time was contiguous

observed_zero_volume_vs_unobserved.observed_zero: an actual archived vendor bar with volume 0 is an OBSERVED zero-volume input
observed_zero_volume_vs_unobserved.unobserved: no source bar for an expected minute

structural_no_trade.consequence: the charter's STRUCTURAL_NO_TRADE state exists and enters RVOL baselines, but this programme cannot yet prove its preconditions, so no minute may be promoted into it
structural_no_trade.baseline_effect: in practice the slot-RVOL baseline is computed over OBSERVED minutes only, and the excluded-minute count must be reported alongside every value

ema_contract.status: DRAFTED_BUT_NOT_FROZEN — blocked by the one_minute_role conflict
ema_contract.time_axis: the ordered sequence of EXPECTED REGULAR minutes for one security across eligible sessions
ema_contract.overnight: non-session time is NOT an expected-minute gap; 15:59 and the next eligible 09:30 may remain consecutive in the regular-market stream
ema_contract.session_policy_note: frozen explicitly rather than left implicit; if the T/Z semantics later require a daily reset, that becomes the authoritative rule
ema_contract.break_rule: an expected REGULAR_WAY minute marked UNOBSERVED BREAKS input continuity; the next observed minute begins a NEW segment
ema_contract.warm_up: no universal threshold is invented here; ema_age_observed_bars is preserved so a downstream contract can require an explicitly pre-registered minimum age
ema_contract.null_policy: unavailable EMA is never a bare NULL; it carries a reason

rvol_contract.label_discipline: the word RVOL is not used until its denominator is fully specified

slot_rvol.numerator: observed volume in minute-of-session slot s of the current session
slot_rvol.denominator: baseline over the same minute-of-session slot s across prior eligible sessions
slot_rvol.lookback_length: TO BE FROZEN IN THE SAME DECISION AS THE EMA RESOLUTION — no value is invented here
slot_rvol.baseline_membership: the per-slot baseline is computed over OBSERVED and STRUCTURAL_NO_TRADE minutes only; UNOBSERVED minutes are excluded from both numerator and denominator
slot_rvol.minimum_sample_count: explicit, uniform, and NOT lowered per security
slot_rvol.zero_denominator: value UNAVAILABLE with reason, never division by zero
slot_rvol.missing_history: excluded from the denominator and counted, never treated as zero volume
slot_rvol.early_close: slot positions come from the XNYS calendar; an early-close session has 210 slots and no post-close slot may be invented

cum_rvol.definition: cumulative session volume relative to the cumulative baseline at the same session position
cum_rvol.contamination: a cumulative curve crossing an UNOBSERVED minute is flagged from that point forward for that session
cum_rvol.flagged_forward: once the curve crosses an UNOBSERVED minute it is flagged from that point forward for that session

rvol_contract.reported_with_every_value: every RVOL-family feature reports the count of excluded UNOBSERVED minutes alongside its value

feature_schemas.ticker: descriptive metadata only; never the primary identity
feature_schemas.provenance_level: FILE_LEVEL — no stronger claim than is implemented

required: UNOBSERVED minute cannot become a zero-volume observation
EMA cannot bridge an UNOBSERVED expected minute silently
EMA unavailable minute cannot be forward-filled
WI bar cannot affect a regular-way feature
NOT_YET bar cannot affect a feature
RVOL denominator cannot use a current or future observation under prior-only semantics
missing historical RVOL input cannot become zero
early-close session cannot create nonexistent late-session positions
feature-unavailable observation cannot silently remove a security from the cohort
a parameter outside the frozen registry must fail
negative_fixtures.standard: each must show the dangerous version FAILS and the correct version PASSES

may_answer: what fraction of expected eligible observations can receive each EMA
how often each EMA resets because of UNOBSERVED minutes
what fraction can receive valid RVOL
RVOL sample counts by minute / session / security
capability_plan.classification: X / DATA CAPABILITY DIAGNOSTIC — not evidence of predictive edge
capability_plan.if_it_changes_parameters: record as pre-Y design provenance and freeze before any Y calculation
capability_plan.why_before_full_build: with 17.7M UNOBSERVED minutes, long-period EMAs may reset often. That would not make a period bad — it would tell us where the feature is actually defined, and we should know that before seeing T/Z

cohort_and_feature_validity.rule: a security is NOT removed from the cohort because a feature is unavailable at some timestamps
cohort_and_feature_validity.separation: cohort membership and feature validity are different dimensions
cohort_and_feature_validity.downstream: analysis may use feature-valid observations only, but must report availability and exclusion accounting

parameter_search_rule.after_freeze: adding another EMA period or RVOL lookback after observing T/Z/Y requires registering a NEW hypothesis family with its own multiplicity and provenance treatment

decision_required: choose option A (build the coarse aggregation layer, then define EMA there) or option B (amend one_minute_role to admit a named 1m-native EMA family). RVOL is unblocked either way.
next_step_if_A: freeze MASSIVE_1M_COARSE_AGGREGATION_SPEC (the charter's aggregation_contract is already detailed), build it, then reissue this feature spec with EMA defined at 15m/1H/1D
